title: Compact CI images and selective build artifact caching
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Background: Our Buildkite pipelines use large, monolithic builder images that include dev-only toolchains, heavy Python wheels, and cached node_modules baked into the image layers. This increases image size, slows distribution across runners, and makes cache invalidation brittle. Goal: reduce CI image footprints and introduce a selective artifact caching strategy that speeds builds and reduces bandwidth/cost without changing developer ergonomics. Scope: audit current builder images, split dev/runtime dependencies into separate images using multi-stage Dockerfiles, enable BuildKit remote cache for reusable layers, implement S3-backed artifact cache for heavy artifacts (wheel builds, compiled assets), and add per-repo cache profiles (fast, normal, full) so repos can opt into different trade-offs.
tasks: Inventory current images across repos and measure compressed size + layer counts
Identify top 10 repos by CI image frequency and bandwidth cost
Prototype multi-stage Dockerfile pattern: runtime-only image + builder-stage with toolchain
Integrate BuildKit/Buildx in Buildkite agents and enable remote layer cache (container registry or S3)
Design per-repo cache profiles and a lightweight YAML schema for opt-in in .buildkite/cache.yml
Add S3-backed artifact cache for Python wheels and compiled assets with TTL and size quotas
Create helper scripts for cache warmup on reusable runners and for CI local dev flow
Migrate 3 pilot repos (api-service, inference-runtime, infra-tooling) and measure wall-clock improvements
Document rollout plan and rollback steps; add observability for cache hit/miss rates in console
acceptance_criteria: Average compressed CI image size reduced by >=40% for pilot repos
Median cold-start build time in Buildkite reduced by >=25% for pilot repos
Cache hit rate >50% within first two weeks for artifacts targeted by the cache profiles
No change required to developer workflow for local builds; documented opt-in for repos wanting aggressive caching
Automated job in ci-monitoring reports cache hit/miss and bandwidth savings weekly
Rollout plan reviewed and approved by infra and security teams
